tldr: A randomized threshold record identifies the causal contrast between two public continuous-dose interventions. On the unchanged unknown-density class, conditionally normalized original-record mixtures prove a finite single-scale lower envelope for absolute risk and finite honest connected-interval length. An explicit safeguarded empirical Galerkin estimator and a public risk-calibrated interval give a closed upper certificate at every sample size. Together they yield a two-sided bracket with \(0<u<e_*\le2/5\). The cubic example rules out the internal quadratic candidate, and the hierarchy excludes uniform root-\(n\) precision; slower finite honest intervals are explicitly available. Sharp mixed-scale rates, logarithms and sharp risk--length equality remain residual questions. The scientific use is a prospective environmental exposure-validation benchmark.
